hypothesis: The exact v39 route set can produce technically valid protected live lifecycles while point-in-time route, regime, execution-friction, and predeclared exit-policy evidence distinguishes repeatable after-cost behavior from whipsaw, profit surrender, and correlated opportunity duplication before a separately versioned $5,000 successor is authorized.
decision: Keep the authorized v39 runtime, routes, entries, position sizing, venue stops, and bound exits unchanged. Record SNDK as a rapid stop-and-recovery whipsaw and SPCX as a cleared-cost-hurdle-then-surrendered lifecycle. Preserve all three previously declared profit-lock policies as report-only measurements, but do not select the best-looking SPCX policy from this one discovery trade, do not install a universal trail, and do not reuse this lifecycle as confirmation evidence. Continue exact route-side observation, regime attribution, missed-opportunity accounting, and independent lifecycle collection before revising the separately versioned $5,000 successor.
falsifier: The technical conclusion is invalidated by changed source identity, unreconciled lifecycle or fill accounting, missing venue protection, a non-causal regime join, or new technical-gap identities. The no-change decision should be revised only by later point-in-time route-specific outcomes showing stable after-cost improvement across non-overlapping episodes, both directional coverage where the route supports both sides, and positive performance without the largest winner. The SPCX exit hypothesis is falsified if any predeclared policy family underperforms the unchanged provider exit after fees, funding, measured exit friction, multiplicity disclosure, and stop precedence on later independent SPCX lifecycles.
limitations: Two resolved lifecycles are not a stable estimate of route or portfolio expectancy, and the four open marks are excluded from resolved decisions.
SNDK and SPCX lack canonical core-regime telemetry; their provider-native context cannot be relabeled with a core-asset regime after the fact.
Selecting one of three profit-lock policies after observing SPCX would incur multiple-testing and discovery-sample bias; all three remain declared measurements.
Counterfactual exits reuse measured lifecycle fee and fill-reference relationships and cannot reproduce a private order that was never submitted.
Mixed-profile all-live evidence is useful for mechanism stress but cannot establish exact-v39 route expectancy.
No live route, position, order, stop, target, size, exit, transition, protection, or execution process changed in this revision.
